title: Ultrafast Third-Harmonic Spectral Modulation And Self-Action In Resonant Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Alfonso Nardi, Sonia Freddi, Michael Scalora, Agostino Di Francescantonio, Johann Osmond, Sofia Martins, Attilio Zilli, Marco Finazzi, Michele Celebrano, Monica Bollani, Maria Antonietta Vincenti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasi-bound states in the continuum enable exceptional field confinement, strongly reducing the pump intensity threshold for nonlinear light-matter interaction in dielectric metasurfaces. As a result, nonlinear self-action effects, often elusive in bulk nonlinear media, emerge at moderate excitation intensities. Here, we show how pulse duration and resonant coupling govern the nonlinear self-action mechanism in resonantly enhanced third-harmonic (TH) generation from a nonlocal metasurface. We identify two excitation regimes that interact differently with the resonant mode, revealing complementary intensity-dependent responses. Under spectrally narrow picosecond excitation, resonance-enhanced TH generation shows pronounced deviations from cubic scaling at high intensities. In contrast, broadband femtosecond excitation transiently drives the resonance, encoding the nonlinear response in the spectral reshaping and broadening of the TH signal. Simulations reproduce both regimes: continuous-wave modeling captures picosecond power scaling and higher-harmonic interactions, while time-domain simulations resolve femtosecond dynamics. These results clarify nonlinear self-action in metasurfaces featuring quasi-bound states in the continuum, linking strong field confinement to conversion efficiency, scaling behavior, and distinct spectral dynamics under different excitation conditions. This work sheds light on the interplay between pulse duration, bandwidth, and resonant coupling in high-Q nonlocal dielectric metasurfaces, advancing their use in ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast third-harmonic generation and nonlinear self-action in resonant nonlocal metasurfaces, focusing on pulse duration and resonant coupling effects.
motivation: To understand how pulse duration and resonant coupling govern nonlinear self-action in high-Q dielectric metasurfaces, which is important for ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics.
method: Experimental measurements of third-harmonic generation under picosecond and femtosecond excitation, supported by continuous-wave and time-domain simulations.
result: Picosecond excitation shows deviations from cubic scaling at high intensities, while femtosecond excitation leads to spectral reshaping and broadening of the third-harmonic signal.
conclusion: The work clarifies nonlinear self-action in metasurfaces with quasi-bound states in the continuum, linking field confinement to conversion efficiency and spectral dynamics.

title: Transition-Set Morphometry For Inter-Scale Contacts In Digital Sandstones
authors: O. M. Kiselev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a transition-set morphometry for quantifying inter-scale contacts in digital sandstones. Pore volume, a medial pore-throat subsystem, and fracture porosity are treated as distinct geometric subsystems. Their finite-neighborhood contacts are represented by transition sets such as [MATH], [MATH], and, when a residual skeleton is resolved, [MATH]. The method measures the density, finite-scale dimension, and weighted contact measures of these sets. A matrix-mode test was performed on 21 digital sandstone samples from the Imperial College micro-CT collection and Digital Porous Media Portal dataset DRP-317. Permeability, expressed as [MATH], served as an external response for assessing how much structural information the descriptors carry. The transition dimension [MATH] alone produced little independent predictive gain, whereas contact measures combining transition-set density with local pore radius were more informative. The adaptive measure [MATH] increased leave-one-out [MATH] from 0.752 to 0.881 in the combined sample and from 0.287 to 0.807 within DRP-317. Fractured datasets DRP-5, DRP-31, and DRP-285 were then used to test the transfer of the same transition-set construction to fracture-related contacts. The results support transition sets as reproducible morphometric descriptors of inter-scale contact.
tldr: This paper introduces a morphometric method for quantifying inter-scale contacts in digital sandstones using transition sets.
motivation: To improve permeability prediction in porous media by characterizing geometric contacts between pore, throat, and fracture subsystems.
method: Defines transition sets to represent finite-neighborhood contacts between distinct geometric subsystems and computes density, dimension, and weighted contact measures.
result: Contact measures combining transition-set density with local pore radius improved leave-one-out R² from 0.752 to 0.881 in combined samples and from 0.287 to 0.807 within a specific dataset.
conclusion: Transition sets are reproducible morphometric descriptors of inter-scale contact that enhance permeability prediction.

title: Avoiding A Line-of-sight Obstacle Via Deep sub-Rayleigh Shadow-projection Utilizing Space-time Wave Packets
authors: Layton A. Hall, Bryan L. Turo, Ayman F. Abouraddy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A challenge in optics, which is shared by other sources of radiation, is to direct a coherent beam to impinge on a target behind an obstacle intervening in the line-of-sight (LoS). While self-accelerating or bending beams can help avoid an LoS obstacle, the beam does not reach the LoS target downstream beyond the obstacle. If one instead avoids the obstacle by projecting a null or shadow onto the axial plane at which it is located, an associated shadow is cast that extends over the effective Rayleigh length, which reduces the utility of this approach. Unless either the wavelength or the transverse shadow width is changed, this Rayleigh length can only be reduced by modifying the structure of the illumination beam. Here we show that space-time wave packets (STWPs), in which each spatial frequency is tightly associated with a single wavelength, when used as an illumination beam, can dramatically reduce the axial extent of the cast shadow. Indeed, by utilizing STWPs we produce deep sub-Rayleigh-length shadows, in some cases with a more than two orders-of-magnitude reduction below the conventional Rayleigh length. For example, a 5-mm-wide transverse shadow in a Gaussian beam at a wavelength of [MATH]~[MATH]m has a Rayleigh length of [MATH]~m, whereas the same shadow projected by an STWP extends only [MATH]~m. We demonstrate this sub-Rayleigh-length reduction in the axially cast shadow accompanying transverse nulls whose widths extend over a broad span of widths from 80~[MATH]m to 48~mm -- almost three orders-of-magnitude. These results may lead to advances in safe radiation therapy, non-LoS optical and wireless communications, selective stand-off detection, three-dimensional photolithography, and laser ablation and micro-machining.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that space-time wave packets can produce deep sub-Rayleigh-length shadows, enabling line-of-sight obstacle avoidance for coherent beams.
motivation: Conventional methods for avoiding line-of-sight obstacles using self-accelerating beams or shadow projection are limited by the Rayleigh length, which restricts the axial extent of the shadow. The authors aim to overcome this limitation using space-time wave packets.
method: The authors use space-time wave packets (STWPs), where each spatial frequency is tightly associated with a single wavelength, to project a null or shadow onto the obstacle plane. They experimentally demonstrate that the axial extent of the shadow is dramatically reduced compared to conventional Gaussian beams.
result: STWPs produce shadows with axial extents more than two orders of magnitude below the conventional Rayleigh length. For example, a 5-mm-wide shadow at a wavelength of ~1.5 μm has a Rayleigh length of ~40 m with a Gaussian beam, but only ~0.4 m with an STWP.
conclusion: The sub-Rayleigh-length shadow projection using STWPs could enable advances in safe radiation therapy, non-line-of-sight communications, selective stand-off detection, and other applications.

title: A New Pbw Basis For The Alternating Central Extension Of The $q$-Onsager Algebra
authors: Haoran Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a new PBW basis for [MATH], the alternating central extension of the [MATH]-Onsager algebra. Terwilliger showed that the alternating generators form a PBW basis in the block order [MATH]. We prove that they also form a PBW basis in the different block order [MATH]. Consequently, multiplication induces a vector-space isomorphism \[ \mathcal W^-\otimes\mathcal G\otimes\otimes\mathcal W^+ \longrightarrow \mathcal A_q, \] thereby confirming a conjecture of Terwilliger.
tldr: This paper establishes a new PBW basis for the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, confirming a conjecture of Terwilliger.
motivation: The q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension are important in the study of exactly solvable models and representation theory. The paper aims to prove that the alternating generators form a PBW basis in a different block order, which was conjectured by Terwilliger.
method: The author constructs a PBW basis by proving that the alternating generators satisfy the required commutation relations and linear independence in the specified block order, using algebraic manipulations and known properties of the algebra.
result: The paper proves that the alternating generators form a PBW basis in the block order W^- ⊗ G ⊗ W^+, and that multiplication induces a vector-space isomorphism from this tensor product to the algebra A_q.
conclusion: The result confirms Terwilliger's conjecture and provides a new PBW basis for the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, contributing to the algebraic structure of these algebras.

title: Mems Fiber-Tip Photoacoustic Spectrometer For In Situ Microscale Trace Gas Sensing
authors: Xingjie Liu, Mengqi Wu, Ping Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To meet the stringent requirements for miniaturized and highly sensitive trace gas sensing in space-constrained scenarios, including power equipment monitoring, minimally invasive biomedical diagnostics, and in situ lithium-battery analysis, we report a MEMS-integrated fiber-tip photoacoustic spectrometer (MFPAS). The device incorporates a Fabry-Perot (F-P) photoacoustic sensor formed by directly butt-coupling a single-mode fiber (SMF) to a 3 mm x 3 mm MEMS chip with a 100-nm-thick low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) Si[MATH]N[MATH] diaphragm. The resulting approximately 200-[MATH]m deep silicon microcavity functions simultaneously as a photoacoustic gas cell and an acoustic confinement cavity. A micro-aperture fabricated at the diaphragm periphery by focused ion beam (FIB) milling serves as both a gas diffusion channel and an acoustic high-pass filter, suppressing ambient low-frequency pressure fluctuations and stabilizing the F-P quadrature point without active servo control. In gas-phase measurements, the sensor achieves a noise-equivalent concentration (NEC) of 58.5 ppb@1s, with a rapid response time of 6 s. Benefiting from its ultra-small cavity volume of approximately 1.5 nL, the device is further adapted through structural packaging for in situ dissolved gas analysis in transformer oil, where it achieves an NEC of 230 ppb@1s and a T90 response time of 320 s in the oil phase. By combining nanoliter-scale detection volume, ppb-level sensitivity, rapid response, and wafer-scale batch fabrication compatibility, the proposed MFPAS bridges MEMS diaphragm micromachining and FIB-enabled gas exchange engineering. This design overcomes the intrinsic gas-exchange limitation of conventional sealed-diaphragm optical microphones and offers significant potential for power equipment monitoring and in situ health diagnostics.
tldr: This paper presents a MEMS fiber-tip photoacoustic spectrometer for trace gas sensing, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve miniaturized and highly sensitive trace gas sensing for applications like power equipment monitoring and biomedical diagnostics.
method: A Fabry-Perot photoacoustic sensor is formed by butt-coupling a single-mode fiber to a MEMS chip with a silicon nitride diaphragm, using a micro-aperture for gas exchange and acoustic filtering.
result: The sensor achieves a noise-equivalent concentration of 58.5 ppb at 1s in gas phase and 230 ppb at 1s in oil phase, with rapid response times.
conclusion: The device bridges MEMS micromachining and FIB-enabled gas exchange, offering potential for in situ health diagnostics and power equipment monitoring.

title: Free-space Multipass Optical Parametric Amplifier
authors: Milan Fayat, Giovanni Cichelli, Michele Natile, Yoann Zaouter, Marie Ouill\'e, Patrick Georges, Marc Hanna, Xavier D\'elen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling the efficiency of optical parametric amplifiers (OPAs) without degrading spatio-temporal pulse quality is fundamentally limited by spatio-temporal walk-off, intensity dependent gain, and back-conversion. Here, we numerically and experimentally demonstrate an OPA architecture based on a free-propagating quasi-periodic geometry that overcomes these bottlenecks. Operating within a single nonlinear crystal, the system utilizes pass-by-pass dichroic idler rejection to suppress back-conversion, a birefringent crystal for temporal resynchronization, and free-space diffraction to improve the spatial overlap along propagation. Starting from 1.9 {\mu}J 330 fs pulses at 515 nm and a continuous-wave seed at 783 nm, the generation of 0.8 {\mu}J 160 fs signal pulses at the same wave-length is obtained at a repetition rate of 500 kHz. This simple architecture achieves a 64% quantum efficiency, a 42% pump-to-signal conversion efficiency, and 80 dB of gain while maintaining excellent spatial and temporal quality, providing a scalable platform for ultrafast sources with arbitrary emission wavelengths.
tldr: This paper presents a free-space multipass optical parametric amplifier architecture that achieves high efficiency and gain while maintaining excellent pulse quality.
motivation: Scaling the efficiency of optical parametric amplifiers is limited by spatio-temporal walk-off, gain saturation, and back-conversion; the authors aim to overcome these bottlenecks.
method: They design a quasi-periodic free-space geometry within a single nonlinear crystal, using dichroic idler rejection, birefringent temporal resynchronization, and free-space diffraction to improve spatial overlap.
result: The system generates 0.8 μJ, 160 fs signal pulses at 783 nm from 1.9 μJ, 330 fs pump pulses at 515 nm, achieving 64% quantum efficiency, 42% pump-to-signal conversion efficiency, and 80 dB gain.
conclusion: The architecture provides a scalable platform for ultrafast sources with arbitrary emission wavelengths, demonstrating that multipass free-space designs can overcome fundamental limitations of OPAs.

title: A Combinatorial Sum With Two Complex Parameters
authors: Robert Frontczak Michel Bataille
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article deals with combinatorial identities with two complex parameters. Starting with a fundamental lemma, we derive various polynomial identities, combinatorial sums and related results. For example, we generalize a polynomial identity of Carlitz involving central binomial coefficients and present a second identity of the same nature. Special cases of our findings lead to sums involving Catalan numbers, harmonic numbers, and Fibonacci numbers.
tldr: The paper derives combinatorial identities involving two complex parameters, generalizing known results about binomial coefficients and special numbers.
motivation: The authors aim to extend combinatorial identities to complex parameters, building on classical results by Carlitz and others.
method: Starting from a fundamental lemma, they manipulate series and polynomial identities to derive new combinatorial sums.
result: They obtain generalizations of Carlitz's polynomial identity and new sums involving Catalan, harmonic, and Fibonacci numbers.
conclusion: The work contributes to combinatorial theory but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Elastically Safeguarded Augmented Lagrangian Methods
authors: Ernesto G. Birgin, Alberto de Marchi, Patrick Mehlitz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate, theoretically and numerically, a class of elastically safeguarded augmented Lagrangian methods for nonlinear optimization problems with inequality and equality constraints. Safeguarded augmented Lagrangian methods are known to exhibit substantially stronger global convergence guarantees than their non-safeguarded counterparts, making them attractive in practice. A persistent limitation, however, is that existing methods rely on a fixed safeguard, whose a priori selection can be difficult and inherently limits adaptivity, e.g., with respect to problem scaling. We propose an adaptive safeguarding mechanism that allows the safeguard to grow dynamically, overcoming these drawbacks while preserving the desirable global convergence properties of variants with a fixed safeguard. We further establish complexity bounds in terms of worst-case iteration counts. Numerical experiments comparing ALGENCAN, a state-of-the-art solver with rigid safeguard, against an elastically safeguarded variant thereof confirm that elastic safeguarding yields consistent practical benefits.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive safeguarding mechanism for augmented Lagrangian methods in nonlinear optimization.
motivation: Existing safeguarded augmented Lagrangian methods rely on a fixed safeguard, which is difficult to select a priori and limits adaptivity.
method: The authors introduce an elastic safeguard that grows dynamically, and prove global convergence and complexity bounds.
result: Numerical experiments show that the elastically safeguarded variant outperforms the state-of-the-art solver ALGENCAN with a rigid safeguard.
conclusion: Elastic safeguarding yields consistent practical benefits while preserving desirable convergence properties.

title: Mitigating Numerical Stiffness In Least-Squares Formulations Of Elliptic PDEs For Physics-Informed Neural Networks
authors: Michael Hecht Phil-Alexander Hofmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present theoretical insights into [MATH] residual loss formulations of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for learning solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs). Standard PINN formulations use a multi-term loss functional consisting of interior and boundary loss terms that are based on [MATH]-residuals and discretized as mean square errors (MSE). Imbalanced magnitudes of these terms cause numerical stiffness phenomena, resulting in ill-conditioning and slow convergence. In this work, we analyze discretizations of the [MATH]-norm that are used in the context of elliptic PDEs with arbitrary, nonzero Dirichlet boundary conditions. We prove that these [MATH] discretizations rebalance the PDE loss, improve conditioning, and mitigate stiffness effects compared with the standard MSE discretization. We validate our theoretic results through operator-level experiments with randomly sampled residuals and PINN experiments for the Poisson and stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. These experiments confirm the numerical effectiveness of the proposed rebalancing for elliptic PDEs and, more broadly, for problems with elliptic behavior.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to mitigate numerical stiffness in physics-informed neural networks for elliptic PDEs by rebalancing the loss function using L2 discretizations.
motivation: Standard PINN formulations suffer from numerical stiffness due to imbalanced loss terms, leading to ill-conditioning and slow convergence.
method: The authors analyze L2-norm discretizations for elliptic PDEs with Dirichlet boundary conditions and prove that these rebalance the PDE loss, improving conditioning.
result: Operator-level and PINN experiments for Poisson and Navier-Stokes equations confirm that the proposed rebalancing mitigates stiffness effects.
conclusion: The L2 discretization approach is numerically effective for elliptic PDEs and problems with elliptic behavior.

title: Optimality-Informed Neural Networks For Lunar Landing Trajectory Optimization
authors: Zhenbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops an Optimality-Informed Neural Network (OINN) approach for the energy-optimal, free-final-time powered descent of a lunar lander from any initial position, velocity, and mass within a bounded operating envelope to a fixed landing site with zero terminal velocity. Building on a recent framework that jointly embeds Pontryagin's minimum principle and the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for general nonlinear optimal control, the proposed OINN approach specializes that idea to a lunar landing problem with free time of flight and fixed terminal state. Every boundary and transversality condition is hard-encoded into the network architecture by construction, the closed-form Pontryagin-optimal thrust magnitude and direction law is substituted directly rather than learned, and the remaining state, costate, and an auxiliary value-function output are trained against a physics-residual loss formed entirely from the necessary conditions of optimality, with no precomputed optimal trajectories required. A preliminary theoretical analysis is explored, establishing a stochastic-optimization stationarity guarantee for the offline training procedure, an explicit bound translating the achieved training residual into bounds on touchdown position, touchdown velocity, and flight-time error, and a fixed, input-independent onboard computational and memory cost suitable for real-time deployment. Numerical simulations evaluate the trained policy, with no retraining, against an independently solved indirect-method boundary-value problem at six representative initial states spanning the operating envelope and against eighty additional Monte Carlo simulation runs, demonstrating close agreement with the indirect-method solution and consistently small dynamics and transversality residuals throughout the envelope.
tldr: This paper develops an Optimality-Informed Neural Network for lunar landing trajectory optimization, embedding optimal control theory into the network architecture.
motivation: To achieve real-time, fuel-optimal powered descent guidance for lunar landers without requiring precomputed trajectories or extensive onboard computation.
method: The approach hard-encodes Pontryagin's minimum principle and transversality conditions into the neural network, uses a physics-residual loss from optimality conditions, and substitutes the closed-form thrust law directly.
result: Numerical simulations show close agreement with indirect-method solutions and consistently small residuals across the operating envelope, with fixed computational cost suitable for real-time deployment.
conclusion: The OINN approach provides a viable method for real-time optimal control of lunar landing, but the paper is focused on aerospace engineering and optimal control, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Online Modeling And Sequential Convex Programming For Lunar Landing Trajectory Optimization
authors: Zhenbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a guidance framework for lunar powered descent and landing that combines sequential convex programming (SCP) with real-time online model identification. A nonconvex energy-optimal landing problem is developed and then reformulated into a sequence of convex second-order cone programs (SOCPs) through a change of variables, successive linearization, and a lossless second-order cone relaxation of the thrust direction constraint. An online identification layer, built from a recursive least squares (RLS) filter with exponential forgetting and an exponential moving average (EMA) smoother, estimates unknown gravitational, thrust-scale, and mass-gauging perturbations from noisy navigation measurements and injects a corrected bias term into the dynamics constraint of each convex subproblem at every guidance cycle. Building on this architecture and my prior work in this area, a baseline SCP algorithm and a receding-horizon online SCP algorithm with model identification are developed. Also, I try to explore some theoretical foundations, establishing the losslessness of the convex relaxation, the mean-square stability and convergence of the identification filters, the guaranteed convergence of the SCP iteration, and explicit convergence radius and convergence rate results. Numerical simulations across four perturbation scenarios of increasing complexity are implemented in MATLAB using YALMIP and the ECOS solver. The results show that the proposed online algorithm consistently reduces landing position and velocity error and better tracks the true propellant consumption relative to an uncorrected nominal trajectory, while retaining the predictable convergence and real-time computational properties of convex optimization.
tldr: This paper presents a guidance framework for lunar landing trajectory optimization using sequential convex programming and online model identification.
motivation: To improve the accuracy and robustness of lunar landing guidance under unknown perturbations and noisy measurements.
method: Combines sequential convex programming with recursive least squares and exponential moving average filters for online model identification, reformulating the nonconvex problem into convex second-order cone programs.
result: Numerical simulations show reduced landing position and velocity errors and better propellant consumption tracking compared to uncorrected nominal trajectories.
conclusion: The proposed online algorithm effectively handles perturbations while maintaining real-time computational properties.

title: Nonlinear Parareal-Incomplete Oswr Method For The Coupled Reaction-Diffusion System: Convergence Analysis And Computational Strategies
authors: Nagaiah Chamakuri Gobinda Garai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a development of a nonlinear extension of the Parareal-Incomplete Optimized Schwarz Waveform Relaxation (OSWR) method, aimed at efficiently simulating coupled reaction-diffusion systems, with particular attention to those encountered in cardiac electrophysiology. The strategy leverages the synergy of spatial and temporal decomposition to tackle the computational challenges of large-scale, nonlinear simulations. The proposed approach is accompanied by a comprehensive convergence analysis. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the convergence of the nonlinear Parareal-Incomplete OSWR method. The results showcase its robust convergence behavior across various space-time subdomains, underscoring the method's reliability and effectiveness, especially in complex simulations involving multiple subdomains.
tldr: This paper develops a nonlinear extension of the Parareal-Incomplete OSWR method for simulating coupled reaction-diffusion systems in cardiac electrophysiology.
motivation: Large-scale nonlinear simulations of coupled reaction-diffusion systems, such as those in cardiac electrophysiology, are computationally challenging and require efficient parallel-in-time methods.
method: The authors propose a nonlinear Parareal-Incomplete OSWR method that combines spatial and temporal decomposition, and provide a convergence analysis along with numerical experiments.
result: Numerical experiments confirm the convergence and robust behavior of the method across various space-time subdomains, demonstrating its reliability for complex multi-subdomain simulations.
conclusion: The nonlinear Parareal-Incomplete OSWR method is an effective computational strategy for large-scale coupled reaction-diffusion systems, with potential applications in cardiac modeling.

title: Kernel-based Learning Of Manifold-to-manifold Maps From Scattered Data
authors: Holger Wendland Daniel Fischer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe and analyze new methods for approximating manifold-to-manifold maps using only scattered data information. To this end, we first study kernel-based approximation methods for scalar-valued functions defined on a manifold and derive a new sampling inequality and error estimates for functions from Sobolev spaces. After that, these methods are combined with a closest point projection to reconstruct manifold-to-manifold maps. The new methods are analyzed and error estimates are derived. Finally, numerical examples are given to verify the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper develops kernel-based methods for approximating maps between manifolds from scattered data, with error estimates and numerical examples.
motivation: Many applications require learning maps between manifolds from scattered data, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors combine kernel-based approximation for scalar functions on manifolds with a closest point projection to reconstruct manifold-to-manifold maps.
result: New sampling inequalities and error estimates are derived, and numerical examples verify the theoretical findings.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide a principled way to approximate manifold-to-manifold maps from scattered data with guaranteed accuracy.

title: Pettis Integrability Of Functions With Values In Separable Symmetrically-normed Ideals And Related Norm Estimates
authors: Mihailo Krsti\'c, Matija Milovi\'c, Stefan Milo\v{s}evi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we will investigate Pettis integrability of [MATH]-valued functions. We will study weakly[MATH] integrable [MATH]-valued functions and establish sufficient conditions for such functions to be Pettis integrable as [MATH]-valued functions. In addition, we prove the inequality $[MATH][MATH]\Phi^{(p)}[MATH]p[MATH]\Phi[MATH][MATH][MATH]$ we provide similar estimates of the Pettis norm.
tldr: This paper studies Pettis integrability of functions taking values in separable symmetrically-normed ideals, with norm estimates.
motivation: To understand conditions under which weakly integrable functions with values in certain operator ideals are Pettis integrable.
method: The authors establish sufficient conditions for Pettis integrability and prove inequalities relating the Pettis norm to other norms.
result: Sufficient conditions for Pettis integrability are given, along with norm estimates for the Pettis norm.
conclusion: The paper contributes to functional analysis and operator theory, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Singularities In Multi-Objective Optimization And Their Crossing During Continuation
authors: Arjun Manoj, Michail E. Kavousanakis, Shanqing Liu, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuation methods help trace Pareto sets in multi-objective optimization but are inherently local: a single run traces a single connected branch, requiring multiple restarts to recover disconnected components of Pareto fronts. We show that, for unconstrained bi-objective problems under weighted-sum scalarization, these disconnects can be artifacts of singularities in the scalarization parameter, where the weight [MATH] diverges as the objective gradients become collinear. Recasting Pareto optimality as a nonlinear system, we apply pseudo-arclength continuation to follow the Pareto-critical set, and show that suitable singular reparameterizations allow crossing these singularities in systematically, recovering disconnected branches in a single run. A coordinate-wise projective compactification further provides a unified framework for parameter and decision-space variables. We demonstrate the approach on the ZDT3 benchmark and modifications.
tldr: This paper studies singularities in multi-objective optimization and uses continuation methods to trace disconnected Pareto fronts.
motivation: Continuation methods for multi-objective optimization are inherently local and fail to recover disconnected Pareto fronts in a single run.
method: The authors reformulate Pareto optimality as a nonlinear system, apply pseudo-arclength continuation, and use singular reparameterizations and projective compactification to cross singularities.
result: They demonstrate that disconnected branches of the Pareto set can be recovered in a single continuation run on the ZDT3 benchmark.
conclusion: The proposed approach enables systematic crossing of singularities in weighted-sum scalarization, unifying parameter and decision-space variables.

title: Voltage Stability Kernel: A Cofactor Theory Of Voltage Stability In Lossy Power Systems
authors: Takayuki Ishizaki, Jigen Koizumi, Hiroo Yashiba, Boqiang Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the voltage stability kernel (VSK), a cofactor-based bus-wise representation of voltage stability in lossy power systems. The VSK is defined as the vector of principal cofactors of the voltage stability Laplacian (VSL), a reduced Jacobian that retains voltage source internal angles while eliminating the other variables. We show that the VSK constitutes the left kernel of the VSL, which is typically nonsymmetric in lossy power systems. We also define the voltage stability margin (VSM) as the sum of all VSK components and show that it is equal to the product of all eigenvalues of the VSL except the trivial zero eigenvalue due to phase-shift symmetry. Thus, the VSK provides a bus-wise decomposition of the VSM. Furthermore, the VSK offers an algebraic interpretation of CPF calculations with a fixed slack bus. The singularity of the Jacobian in CPF calculations obtained by deleting the slack-bus row and column is characterized by the vanishing of the VSK component selected by the slack bus. In contrast, the static bifurcation is characterized by the vanishing of the VSM. Since these two conditions are generally different, our theory explains why a CPF nose point does not necessarily correspond to a static bifurcation in lossy cases.
tldr: This paper introduces a cofactor-based representation of voltage stability in lossy power systems, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a bus-wise decomposition of voltage stability margin in power systems, addressing limitations of traditional continuation power flow methods in lossy networks.
method: The authors define the voltage stability kernel (VSK) as the vector of principal cofactors of the voltage stability Laplacian (VSL), a reduced Jacobian, and show it forms the left kernel of the VSL.
result: The VSK provides a bus-wise decomposition of the voltage stability margin (VSM), and the singularity conditions for CPF and static bifurcation are shown to differ in lossy cases.
conclusion: The VSK theory explains why CPF nose points do not necessarily correspond to static bifurcations in lossy power systems.

title: Cram\'er-Rao Bound Optimization For Massive Mimo Dfrc Systems With 1-Bit DACs And ADCs
authors: Chenfei Huang, Mingjie Shao, Ya-Feng Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the dual-function radar-communication (DFRC) design for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems equipped with 1-bit digital-to-analog converters (DACs) at the transmitter and 1-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) at the receiver, motivated by the need for low-cost and power-efficient implementations of massive MIMO systems. We consider a downlink scenario where the transmit signal matrix is optimized to enhance sensing performance while satisfying communication quality of service (QoS) requirements. Specifically, the objective is to minimize the 1-bit Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) for estimating the azimuth angle of a point-like target under symbol-level constructive interference (CI) constraints. We conduct an asymptotic analysis of the 1-bit Fisher information, revealing its nonmonotonicity with the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and introduce amplitude constraints to exclude regions where the objective function value is clearly suboptimal and facilitate convergence to high-quality solutions. The resulting problem is a nonconvex optimization challenge with coupled binary and linear constraints. We transform the discrete problem into a continuous constrained one, characterize its global and local minima, and tackle it via the augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) and a spectral projected gradient (SPG) method combined with nonmonotone line search. The solution is further refined via local search and cutting-plane techniques. Extensive numerical experiments verify our analysis, showing that the proposed approach exhibits promising DFRC performance compared to benchmark schemes.
tldr: This paper optimizes Cramér-Rao bound for massive MIMO DFRC systems with 1-bit DACs/ADCs, focusing on radar sensing and communication trade-offs.
motivation: Low-cost and power-efficient massive MIMO systems require 1-bit converters, but this introduces challenges in dual-function radar-communication design.
method: The authors formulate a nonconvex optimization problem to minimize the 1-bit CRB under constructive interference constraints, using asymptotic analysis, augmented Lagrangian method, and spectral projected gradient with local search.
result: Numerical experiments show the proposed approach achieves promising DFRC performance compared to benchmarks.
conclusion: The paper provides a practical optimization framework for DFRC with coarse quantization, but is purely in classical signal processing and communications.

title: A Geometric Local Parameterization Method For Generalized Hele-Shaw Free Boundary Problems With Source Terms
authors: Zengyan Zhang, Wenrui Hao, John Harlim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a meshfree numerical framework for Hele--Shaw free boundary problems with surface tension and source terms based on geometric local parameterization and boundary integral methods. By decomposing the pressure into a particular solution and a harmonic component, the problem is reformulated into a boundary-only system, avoiding volumetric meshing of the evolving domain. For general source terms, we propose an eigenfunction-based approximation on a fixed domain and establish error estimates for both the truncation and coefficient approximation. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and convergence of the proposed method, and an application to a tumor growth model demonstrates its effectiveness for coupled moving-boundary problems.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical method for Hele-Shaw free boundary problems with source terms, applied to tumor growth modeling.
motivation: Hele-Shaw problems with surface tension and source terms are challenging to solve numerically; existing methods require volumetric meshing which is computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose a meshfree framework using geometric local parameterization and boundary integral methods, decomposing pressure into a particular solution and a harmonic component to obtain a boundary-only system.
result: Error estimates for truncation and coefficient approximation are established, and numerical experiments verify accuracy and convergence; an application to tumor growth demonstrates effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an efficient and accurate approach for simulating Hele-Shaw free boundary problems with source terms, particularly useful for coupled moving-boundary problems like tumor growth.

title: Direct Sampling Methods For Inverse Interface Problems
authors: Kazufumi Ito, Tong Wu, Jun Zou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates two types of inverse interface problems in scenarios where only very limited Cauchy data is available. These problems are associated with the Laplace equation featuring a Robin-type flux jump across an internal interface. The first problem focuses on reconstructing the location of cracks along a known interface using Cauchy data measured on the outer boundary. The second problem involves determining the location of an unknown interface based on Cauchy data from the outer boundary. To address these challenges, we adopt an efficient Direct Sampling Method (DSM) and introduce innovative enhancements to the boundary conditions in the reference system, thereby maximizing the utility of the available Cauchy data. Additionally, we propose a novel refinement to further improve the robustness of the DSM against noise. We provide a detailed exposition of the general principles underlying the DSM and systematically present its computational implementation steps. Through detailed Fourier analysis and computations, we illustrate the theoretical background of the DSM as well as the effectiveness of our refinement approach. A series of numerical experiments demonstrates that our method yields highly satisfactory results, even when processing incomplete and noisy Cauchy data on the outer boundary. We introduce quantitative metrics, such as Mean Localization Error (MLE) and Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (CNR), to rigorously evaluate the performance of our method. These findings underscore the exceptional effectiveness and broad applicability of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper develops direct sampling methods for inverse interface problems in Laplace equations with limited Cauchy data.
motivation: Inverse interface problems arise in applications like crack detection and interface identification, but are challenging when only limited boundary data is available.
method: The authors propose a Direct Sampling Method (DSM) with enhanced boundary conditions and a refinement to improve robustness against noise, supported by Fourier analysis.
result: Numerical experiments show the method achieves high accuracy even with incomplete and noisy data, quantified by Mean Localization Error and Contrast-to-Noise Ratio.
conclusion: The proposed DSM is effective and broadly applicable for reconstructing interfaces from limited Cauchy data.

title: A Proximal Point Semismooth Newton Algorithm For Structural Composite Cardinality Optimization
authors: Penghe Zhang, Naihua Xiu, Houduo Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many image-processing problems can be formulated as composite cardinality optimization (CCOP), whose objective is the sum of two convex terms and a cardinality function composed with a linear operator. The composite cardinality term creates major algorithmic challenges: the separability of the cardinality function is lost and convergence analysis often requires surjectivity-type assumptions on the linear operators. To overcome these challenges, we consider the stationary dual formulation of CCOP, which has more favorable structure consisting of two convex terms and a separable cardinality function. In this paper, we develop an efficient proximal point algorithm (PPA) to solve the stationary dual problem. The efficiency of our PPA stems from two aspects. Firstly, the key step of its subproblem solver minimizes a smooth convex function over a low-dimensional subspace by the classic semismooth Newton algorithm (SNA), which has global convergence and local superlinear rate under suitable conditions. Secondly, implementable inexact criteria are proposed for early termination of the SNA subroutine. These components form the basic framework of our inexact PPA. Under suitable conditions, it enjoys global convergence and local linear convergence rate. In particular, we provide examples in which the convergence assumptions are automatically satisfied. Finally, the SNA subroutine is incorporated into our inexact PPA to solve jump-sparse signal recovery and computed tomography (CT) image restoration. Numerical results demonstrate the time efficiency and solution accuracy of our proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a proximal point semismooth Newton algorithm for solving composite cardinality optimization problems in image processing.
motivation: Composite cardinality optimization problems arise in image processing but are challenging due to non-separability and surjectivity assumptions; the authors aim to develop an efficient algorithm.
method: The algorithm solves a stationary dual formulation with a separable cardinality function using a proximal point method, where the subproblem is solved by a semismooth Newton algorithm on a low-dimensional subspace.
result: The algorithm achieves global convergence and local linear convergence under suitable conditions, and numerical experiments on jump-sparse signal recovery and CT image restoration demonstrate time efficiency and accuracy.
conclusion: The proposed inexact PPA with SNA subroutine is effective for composite cardinality optimization, with theoretical guarantees and practical performance.

title: Subspace Curvature-scaling High-index Saddle Dynamics For Accelerating Ill-conditioned Saddle Point Searches
authors: Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang, Zhiyi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a subspace curvature-scaling high-index saddle dynamics (SCS-HiSD) method to accelerate high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) for locating ill-conditioned saddle points. The key observation is that HiSD already computes approximations of the unstable Hessian eigenvectors during iteration, which can be used at negligible additional cost to construct an inverse-Hessian approximation on the unstable subspace. This subspace curvature information is incorporated to adaptively scale the dynamics along each unstable direction, eliminating the dependence of the convergence rate on the smallest-magnitude negative eigenvalues and thereby substantially accelerating the convergence for ill-conditioned saddle points. We establish the linear stability of the continuous SCS-HiSD system and provide a local convergence analysis for the discrete iterative scheme. This method extends naturally to address slow convergence caused by small positive eigenvalues. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems and a liquid-crystal model demonstrate that SCS-HiSD substantially accelerates the computation of ill-conditioned saddle points, particularly in severely ill-conditioned cases.
tldr: This paper proposes a numerical optimization method for accelerating saddle point searches in ill-conditioned systems, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) converges slowly for ill-conditioned saddle points due to small-magnitude negative eigenvalues. The authors aim to accelerate convergence by leveraging subspace curvature information.
method: The method uses approximations of unstable Hessian eigenvectors computed during HiSD iterations to construct an inverse-Hessian scaling on the unstable subspace, adaptively scaling the dynamics along each unstable direction.
result: Numerical experiments on benchmark problems and a liquid-crystal model show substantial acceleration, especially in severely ill-conditioned cases.
conclusion: The subspace curvature-scaling approach effectively eliminates the dependence on smallest-magnitude negative eigenvalues, significantly speeding up saddle point searches.

title: Propagation Direction Near The Strong-Competition Borderline In The Two-Species Lotka-Volterra Model
authors: Shun-Chieh Wang Chiun-Chuan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates the propagation direction of bistable traveling waves in the two-species Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion model under strong competition. From an ecological perspective, the sign of the wave speed is critical, as it dictates which species eventually prevails. We focus on a near-symmetric scenario where intrinsic growth rates and inter-specific competition coefficients are identical, leaving diffusion rates as the sole source of asymmetry. This framework is motivated by the conjecture "Unity is not strength" as described by Alzahrani et al., Girardin and Nadin, and Girardin, which proposes that the species with the higher diffusion rate gains a competitive advantage, directly dictating the wave speed's sign. While extensive literature, including the significant recent progress by Nakamura and Ogiwara, has validated this conjecture under specific assumptions, a comprehensive proof remains elusive. In this paper, we explore the subtle regime where inter-specific competition weakens, approaching the strong-competition borderline. Leveraging our previous finding, a minimax formulation for the zero-wave-speed condition, we successfully analyze the asymptotic behavior of the wave and construct a sharp test function to determine the sign of the wave speed. Consequently, we verify "Unity is not strength" conjecture within this new parameter regime and derive explicit bounds that characterize how the zero-wave-speed condition is influenced by the interplay between competition strength and diffusion rates.
tldr: This paper studies propagation direction of bistable traveling waves in a two-species Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion model, focusing on the strong-competition borderline.
motivation: To determine which species prevails in a competitive ecosystem when diffusion rates are asymmetric, testing the 'Unity is not strength' conjecture.
method: Uses a minimax formulation for zero-wave-speed condition and constructs a sharp test function to analyze asymptotic behavior of the wave.
result: Verifies the conjecture in the near-strong-competition regime and derives explicit bounds on how competition strength and diffusion rates affect wave speed.
conclusion: The species with higher diffusion rate gains a competitive advantage, confirming the conjecture under the studied parameter regime.

title: The Clarke Tangent And Normal Cones To Decomposable Sets In Lebesgue Spaces
authors: Petar Evgeniev

tldr: This paper studies Clarke tangent and normal cones for decomposable sets in Lebesgue spaces, with applications to nonsmooth optimization and integral functionals.
motivation: The paper aims to extend variational analysis tools to decomposable sets in function spaces, which are important for optimization problems with constraints that are pointwise in nature.
method: The author defines and characterizes the Clarke tangent cone for decomposable sets in L^p spaces using measurable multifunctions, and derives corresponding normal cones.
result: Explicit formulas for the tangent and normal cones are obtained for 1 ≤ p < ∞, with partial results for p = ∞. Applications to constrained optimization and Nemytskii operators are discussed.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for nonsmooth analysis on decomposable sets, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Finite Element Approximation Of The Enthalpy Formulation For Stefan Problems On Evolving Surfaces
authors: Philip J. Herbert, Thomas Sales, Chandrasekhar Venkataraman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose, and analyse, a spatially discrete evolving surface finite element method for the approximation of the enthalpy formulation of the two-phase Stefan problem posed on an evolving surface. Our approach does not rely on mass-lumping and discrete maximum principles. We prove this numerical method is numerically stable, and prove [MATH] error bounds for the temperature in the [MATH] norm under minimal regularity assumptions by introducing a new projection-type operator. We complement our analysis with discussion on the implementation of this numerical method, where we propose a novel implementation that avoids errors due to numerical quadrature and which has not previously been considered in the literature even in the stationary, flat setting. We also include numerical experiments and experimental order of convergence demonstrations.
tldr: This paper develops a finite element method for Stefan problems on evolving surfaces, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to numerically solve two-phase Stefan problems on evolving surfaces, a classical problem in computational mathematics.
method: An evolving surface finite element method is proposed for the enthalpy formulation, avoiding mass-lumping and discrete maximum principles, with a new projection operator for error analysis.
result: The method is proven numerically stable with optimal error bounds, and a novel implementation avoids quadrature errors.
conclusion: The work contributes to numerical analysis of moving boundary problems but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Relative Periodic Orbits In The Spatial Anisotropic Kepler Problem
authors: Xijun Hu, Yuwei Ou, Zhiwen Qiao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spatial anisotropic Kepler problem comes from quantum mechanics, which models electron motion in semiconductors with donor impurities and depends on the anisotropic parameter [MATH]. After reducing the system modulo rotational symmetry, we investigate periodic orbits in this two-degree-of-freedom setting. Combining an index comparison in , the volume formula in and Franks' theorem, we prove that the system possesses infinitely many periodic orbits on any fixed compact and regular energy surface for [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies periodic orbits in the spatial anisotropic Kepler problem, a classical mechanics problem derived from quantum mechanics.
motivation: The anisotropic Kepler problem models electron motion in semiconductors with donor impurities, and understanding its periodic orbits is important for quantum mechanics.
method: The authors reduce the system modulo rotational symmetry, then combine an index comparison, volume formula, and Franks' theorem to prove existence of infinitely many periodic orbits.
result: They prove that on any fixed compact and regular energy surface for a certain parameter range, there are infinitely many periodic orbits.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous dynamical systems analysis of a model originating from quantum mechanics, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Adaptive Linear Quadratic Control Of Unknown Linear Time-Varying Systems Via Policy Gradient Methods
authors: Florian D\"orfler Feiran Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unknown linear time-varying (LTV) systems require the control policy to adapt from online closed-loop data as dynamics evolve. Existing methods usually update the policy by solving a one-shot optimization problem, which can be computationally demanding and sensitive to noisy model estimates. In this paper, we propose a policy gradient adaptive control (PGAC) method for LTV system control with unknown model parameters. Specifically, PGAC integrates online policy optimization into feedback by updating the state-feedback policy with one-step gradient descent of the linear quadratic regulator cost at each time instant. This incremental update is computationally light and naturally limits policy variations caused by noisy data. To explicitly compute the policy gradient online, we estimate local models from recent closed-loop trajectories using normalized sliding-window least-squares. We provide stability and convergence certificates of PGAC for two classes of LTV systems. For slowly time-varying systems, we prove that the closed-loop system achieves practical exponential stability without a dwell-time condition. For piecewise-constant LTV systems, we establish practical stability through a dwell-time contraction argument. We also provide average frozen-time optimality-gap bounds of the policy sequence for both classes. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our method via numerical case studies of both LTV and nonlinear systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a policy gradient adaptive control method for unknown linear time-varying systems, focusing on stability and optimality guarantees.
motivation: Existing adaptive control methods for LTV systems are computationally demanding and sensitive to noise; a lightweight online policy update is needed.
method: The method integrates online policy optimization with one-step gradient descent of the LQR cost, using sliding-window least-squares for local model estimation.
result: Practical exponential stability for slowly time-varying systems and practical stability for piecewise-constant systems are proven, with average optimality-gap bounds.
conclusion: The proposed PGAC method is computationally efficient and provides stability certificates, validated on LTV and nonlinear systems.

title: An Onsager Variational Scheme For Pressure-Driven Tumor Growth And Hele-Shaw Limits
authors: Xinran Ruan Weijie Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pressure-driven tumor growth models describe the coupling between cell proliferation and mechanical pressure and naturally lead to moving free boundary problems. Their numerical approximation is challenging due to degenerate diffusion, pressure-dependent proliferation, and the stiffness of the pressure law \(p=n^\gamma\) for large \(\gamma\). In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving finite difference method for this class of pressure-driven tumor growth models with pressure-dependent proliferation. The method is derived from the Onsager variational principle. The key idea is to introduce a modified energy shifted by the homeostatic pressure, so that the growth term can be written in a dissipative form and incorporated together with the transport part into a unified Rayleighian formulation. This formulation leads to a time-discrete constrained minimization problem and a fully discrete scheme with explicit mobilities and an implicit pressure update. We prove that the scheme preserves nonnegativity and the homeostatic upper bound, satisfies a discrete modified energy dissipation law, and admits a fixed-grid stiff-pressure limiting structure. Numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions demonstrate the accuracy of the method, its convergence toward the Hele--Shaw limit for large \(\gamma\), and its ability to capture free boundary evolutions with topology changes.
tldr: This paper proposes a structure-preserving finite difference method for pressure-driven tumor growth models using the Onsager variational principle.
motivation: Numerical approximation of pressure-driven tumor growth models is challenging due to degenerate diffusion, pressure-dependent proliferation, and stiffness of the pressure law.
method: The method introduces a modified energy shifted by homeostatic pressure, leading to a unified Rayleighian formulation and a time-discrete constrained minimization problem.
result: The scheme preserves nonnegativity and homeostatic upper bound, satisfies a discrete modified energy dissipation law, and converges to the Hele-Shaw limit for large γ.
conclusion: The proposed method accurately captures free boundary evolutions with topology changes and is validated in 1D and 2D numerical experiments.

title: Accelerating Droplet-laden Stokes Flow Simulations With Hierarchical Surrogate Modeling
authors: Davide Pradovera, Thomas Frachon, Sara Zahedi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a surrogate modeling strategy for Stokes flows with liquid droplets suspended in a carrier fluid. Our approach is based on a multi-fidelity framework. At the lowest fidelity, droplets are treated as passive tracers, neglecting their influence on the ambient flow field. Building on this approximation, we derive a PDE that represents the current modeling error. This error equation is then solved approximately to correct the flow field and the procedure is iterated. Two fidelities are employed in an alternating fashion: Stokes flow in the absence of droplets and flow around a single droplet in free space. By systematically combining these models, the method captures droplet-flow, droplet-boundary, and droplet-droplet interactions. For geometrically similar droplets, we further develop an efficient offline-online strategy that exploits this structure by reusing precomputed single-droplet solutions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed surrogate in a variety of tests, including scenarios with up to 10,000 droplets. Notably, we show that the proposed surrogate achieves substantially reduced computational cost compared to fully resolved multi-fluid simulations with state-of-the-art software.
tldr: This paper presents a surrogate modeling strategy for accelerating Stokes flow simulations with suspended droplets, using a multi-fidelity framework.
motivation: Fully resolved multi-fluid simulations of droplet-laden flows are computationally expensive, motivating the need for efficient surrogate models.
method: A hierarchical surrogate is built by alternating between a low-fidelity model (droplets as passive tracers) and a high-fidelity correction derived from a PDE representing the modeling error, with an offline-online strategy for geometrically similar droplets.
result: The surrogate achieves substantial computational cost reduction compared to fully resolved simulations, demonstrated in tests with up to 10,000 droplets.
conclusion: The proposed multi-fidelity approach effectively captures droplet-flow, droplet-boundary, and droplet-droplet interactions while significantly reducing computational cost.

title: Robust Transitivity Of Geodesic Flows From Metrics With Conjugate Points
authors: Ygor de Jesus, Luis Pedro Pi\~neyr\'ua, Sergio Roma\~na
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove a general criterion for obtaining robust transitivity of partially hyperbolic geodesic flows. As a consequence, we exhibit the first example of a [MATH] open set of Riemannian metrics with conjugate points and transitive geodesic flow. In particular, such a set does not intersect the set of Riemannian metrics with Anosov geodesic flows.
tldr: This paper proves a criterion for robust transitivity of partially hyperbolic geodesic flows and exhibits the first open set of Riemannian metrics with conjugate points and transitive geodesic flow.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of geodesic flows on manifolds with conjugate points, which are not Anosov.
method: The authors develop a general criterion for robust transitivity of partially hyperbolic geodesic flows and apply it to construct an example.
result: They obtain the first open set of Riemannian metrics with conjugate points and transitive geodesic flow, which does not intersect the set of Anosov geodesic flows.
conclusion: This advances the study of geodesic flows beyond the Anosov setting, showing that transitivity can occur robustly even with conjugate points.

title: Convergence Of Substructuring Waveform Relaxation Algorithms For Hyperbolic PDEs With Time Delay
authors: Deeksha Tomer Bankim Chandra Mandal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article investigates the application and analysis of two substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms namely Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (DNWR) and Neumann-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (NNWR) for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) with time delay. These equations are relevant in numerous physical and engineering contexts, such as wave propagation, biological processes, and control systems, where the system's dynamics are influenced by past states. The study emphasizes the stability, convergence, and computational efficiency of these non-overlapping domain decomposition methods when applied to such problems. Specifically, the DNWR and NNWR algorithms are analyzed using both Fourier and Laplace transforms in asymmetric domain decomposition to assess their capability to manage delayed terms in hyperbolic systems. Using Fourier analysis, we establish linear convergence estimate for the numerical errors. Laplace transform analysis enables a more in-depth study for characterizing finite-step convergence. Additionally, we derive the optimal parameters required to achieve finite step convergence in presence of heterogeneous spatial domain. Theoretical findings are complemented by numerical experiments, showcasing the methods' effectiveness in maintaining accuracy while reducing computational complexity. Additionally, the study explores potential extensions to more complex problems and diverse applications.
tldr: This paper analyzes waveform relaxation algorithms for hyperbolic PDEs with time delay, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to improve computational efficiency for solving hyperbolic PDEs with time delay, relevant in engineering and physics but not quantum information.
method: The authors apply Dirichlet-Neumann and Neumann-Neumann waveform relaxation methods, using Fourier and Laplace transforms to analyze convergence.
result: Linear convergence estimates and optimal parameters for finite-step convergence are derived, with numerical experiments confirming effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed methods are effective for the targeted PDEs, but the work has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Bhep Test For Multivariate Normality On Incomplete Data
authors: Philipp W\"ubbolding Daniel Gaigall
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A BHEP test for the null hypotesis of multivariate normality on the basis of incomplete data is introduced. Estimators for the underlying unknown parameters in this situation are suggested. The test uses characteristic functions and circumvents the problem of singular covariance matrix estimates. As the sample size tends to infinity, an almost sure limit of the test statistic is obtained under the null hypothesis and under alternatives. The convergence in distribution under the null hypothesis is also proved. Critical values can be obtained using a bootstrap procedure. Simulation studies investigate size and power of the test and confirm the adequacy of the approach. A real data example demonstrates the application of the test.
tldr: This paper proposes a BHEP test for multivariate normality on incomplete data, using characteristic functions and a bootstrap procedure.
motivation: Testing multivariate normality is important in statistics, but existing methods often require complete data. This work addresses the case of incomplete data, which is common in practice.
method: The test uses characteristic functions to avoid singular covariance matrix estimates, and critical values are obtained via bootstrap. Asymptotic properties are proved.
result: The test statistic converges almost surely under null and alternatives, and converges in distribution under the null. Simulations show good size and power.
conclusion: The proposed test is a valid and practical method for testing multivariate normality with incomplete data.

title: An LSQR-based Algorithm For Large-scale Null Space Computations
authors: Jinzhi Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing the null space and null vectors of large-scale matrices is a fundamental task in numerical linear algebra and scientific computing. In this paper, an LSQR-based algorithm, termed LSQRNV, is proposed to compute a null vector of a large rank-deficient matrix [MATH] from an initial vector. Theoretical convergence properties of the algorithm are analyzed, and an accuracy bound is derived for the computed approximate null vector. By integrating a deflation technique with a specialized termination criterion, LSQRNV is extended to LSQRNS, which computes an orthonormal basis for the null space [MATH] and explicitly determines the nullity of [MATH]. A rigorous accuracy bound is established for the resulting approximate numerical null space. Furthermore, with appropriate parameter settings, LSQRNV efficiently determines whether a large matrix is numerically rank-deficient or has full column rank. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical results, demonstrating the robustness, efficiency, and effectiveness of LSQRNS for large-scale null-space computation.
tldr: This paper presents an LSQR-based algorithm for computing null spaces of large-scale matrices, a topic in numerical linear algebra.
motivation: Computing null spaces of large matrices is fundamental in scientific computing, but existing methods may be inefficient for large-scale problems.
method: The authors propose LSQRNV, an LSQR-based algorithm to compute a null vector, and extend it to LSQRNS using deflation to compute an orthonormal basis for the null space.
result: Theoretical convergence and accuracy bounds are derived, and numerical experiments demonstrate robustness and efficiency for large-scale null-space computation.
conclusion: LSQRNS is an effective and robust algorithm for large-scale null-space computations, with rigorous accuracy guarantees.

title: Dynamic Congestion Pricing In Distribution Networks Via A Convex-Analytic Bilevel Reformulation
authors: Reza Rahimi Baghbadorani, Ali Nikseresht, Jehum Cho, Yashar Ghiassi-Farrokhfal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic congestion pricing is an important tool for managing congestion and coordinating distributed energy resources in active distribution networks. However, scalable mechanisms that preserve participant autonomy remain computationally challenging because the operator-resource interaction is naturally bilevel. This paper develops a convex-analytic framework in which a distribution system operator computes dynamic congestion-price adders, while decentralized energy hubs schedule flexible demand, storage, local generation, renewable curtailment, and grid import/export. Unlike conventional single-level reformulations that replace lower-level problems by Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, complementarity constraints, and big-M linearizations, the proposed model represents follower feasibility and optimality through a Fenchel-Young equality involving the convex conjugate of an extended follower objective. The remaining bilinear price-response term is handled through a penalized difference-of-convex reformulation and sequential convex approximation. The method solves continuous convex subproblems and avoids the constraint-wise complementarity and branch-and-bound scaling of mixed-integer KKT reformulations; its main computational drivers are price-response dimension and conjugate evaluation rather than binary encodings of follower inequalities. On augmented IEEE 13- and 34-node feeders, it reduces congestion by 96.89% and 96.45%, respectively, approaches centralized full-information dispatch, certifies price-response consistency to numerical precision, and yields lower residual congestion than time-limited KKT incumbents within the computational budget.
tldr: This paper proposes a convex-analytic bilevel optimization framework for dynamic congestion pricing in power distribution networks.
motivation: Dynamic congestion pricing is important for managing congestion and coordinating distributed energy resources, but existing bilevel optimization methods are computationally challenging due to mixed-integer formulations.
method: The authors reformulate the bilevel problem using Fenchel-Young equality and convex conjugate, handle bilinear terms via penalized difference-of-convex reformulation and sequential convex approximation, solving continuous convex subproblems.
result: On IEEE 13- and 34-node feeders, the method reduces congestion by 96.89% and 96.45%, respectively, approaching centralized dispatch performance with lower residual congestion than time-limited KKT incumbents.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a scalable and computationally efficient alternative to traditional KKT-based bilevel methods for dynamic congestion pricing in distribution networks.

title: Generalized Idempotents On The Space Of Analytic Functions With Bounded Derivatives
authors: Himanshu Kumar, Abdullah Bin Abu Baker, Fernanda Botelho
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a complex normed space. A map [MATH] is called idempotent if [MATH]. A collection [MATH] of nonzero distinct orthogonal ([MATH]) idempotent maps on [MATH] is said to be a family of generalized bi-circular idempotents if there exist distinct unit modulus complex numbers [MATH] such that [MATH] (identity operator on [MATH]) and [MATH] is a surjective isometry on [MATH]. This generalizes the notion of generalized bi-circular projections on Banach spaces introduced by Foner, Ilievi\'{c} and Li to nonlinear maps. In this paper, we describe the structure of generalized bi-circular idempotents over the space of analytic functions on the open unit disk with bounded derivatives.
tldr: This paper studies generalized bi-circular idempotents on the space of analytic functions with bounded derivatives, a topic in functional analysis.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the concept of generalized bi-circular projections from linear maps to nonlinear idempotent maps on certain function spaces.
method: They characterize the structure of families of orthogonal idempotent maps satisfying a specific linear combination condition involving a surjective isometry.
result: The paper describes the explicit form of such generalized bi-circular idempotents on the space of analytic functions on the unit disk with bounded derivatives.
conclusion: This work generalizes known results on bi-circular projections to a nonlinear setting, contributing to the theory of idempotents on function spaces.

title: Optimal Mean-time Path Planning For Unmanned Underwater Vehicles: A Hamilton-Jacobi Approach
authors: Jonathan Valyou, Jeremy Brandman, Sanghyun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unmanned underwater vehicles (UUV) integrate ocean forecasts with path planning algorithms in order to identify energy- or time-minimizing paths that enable mission completion. Typically, a well-defined deterministic ocean forecast is assumed to be available for path planning; however, in practice, different ocean forecasts can disagree. In this paper, we extend previous work on deterministic optimal path planning to identify optimal mean-time paths when presented with an ensemble of possible ocean forecasts. In particular, we formulate a system of time-independent Hamilton-Jacobi partial differential equations that incorporates forecast uncertainty and yields the optimal mean reachability travel time and the necessary controls to find the associated optimal path. An efficient numerical solution of this system of PDEs is obtained through an extension of the Fast Sweeping Method; verification and benchmarking results are provided. Additional numerical examples illustrate the impact uncertainty can have on the optimal path; in particular, these results demonstrate that the vehicle's optimal path can deviate significantly from the deterministic optimal paths associated with the individual ensemble members.
tldr: This paper presents a Hamilton-Jacobi approach for optimal mean-time path planning for unmanned underwater vehicles under forecast uncertainty.
motivation: Unmanned underwater vehicles need energy- or time-minimizing paths, but deterministic ocean forecasts can disagree, so a method that accounts for forecast uncertainty is needed.
method: The authors formulate a system of time-independent Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs that incorporate forecast uncertainty and solve it efficiently using an extension of the Fast Sweeping Method.
result: Numerical examples show that the optimal path under uncertainty can deviate significantly from deterministic optimal paths based on individual ensemble members.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a way to compute optimal mean-time paths that are robust to forecast uncertainty, improving mission planning for UUVs.

title: Asynchronous Sensitivity-Based Distributed Nmpc
authors: Maximilian Pierer von Esch, Andres V\"olz, Knut Graichen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a cooperative distributed model predictive control (MPC) scheme for nonlinear continuous-time systems. The centralized optimal control problem is solved asynchronously via a fixed number of sensitivity-based distributed programming (SBDP) iterations. The proposed scheme requires only neighbor-to-neighbor communication and no synchronization between agents during optimization. Under nominal MPC stability and bounded information delay, local exponential stability is established for a sufficiently large number of per-agent SBDP iterations. Numerical and hardware-in-the-loop results on both Ethernet and Wi-Fi demonstrate the benefits of an asynchronous execution, reducing execution times by over 60% while maintaining comparable closed loop performance.
tldr: This paper presents an asynchronous sensitivity-based distributed model predictive control scheme for nonlinear continuous-time systems.
motivation: To reduce execution time and communication overhead in distributed MPC by allowing asynchronous updates without requiring synchronization between agents.
method: The centralized optimal control problem is solved asynchronously via a fixed number of sensitivity-based distributed programming iterations, requiring only neighbor-to-neighbor communication.
result: Local exponential stability is established for sufficiently many iterations, and numerical and hardware-in-the-loop experiments show over 60% reduction in execution time with comparable performance.
conclusion: Asynchronous execution in distributed MPC can significantly improve efficiency while maintaining stability and performance.

title: Coalesced Matrix-Free Geometric Multigrid On Persistent Cell-Wise Storage
authors: Micha{\l} Wichrowski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.03413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a geometric multigrid preconditioner for high-order continuous finite elements that operates entirely on redundant, cell-wise stored vectors: the assembled global vector is never formed on any level of the hierarchy. In this storage paradigm the machinery that classically complicates adaptive multigrid dissolves. Hanging-node constraints are never assembled: we prove that the plain tensor-product transfer operators, applied to the residual, algebraically reproduce the classical constrained restriction, including the action of the transposed constraint matrix, and the edge operators of local smoothing reduce to a pointwise masking of the residual, with no splitting of the level operator into interior and edge blocks. As a consequence, the single inter-cell primitive of the whole V-cycle can use a topologically oblivious structured kernel even on adaptively refined meshes.
